profile.campus: Sunnyvale, California (Equinix SV6, Silicon Valley network)
profile.reading:
Equinix SV6 sits at 444 Toyama Drive in the Lakewood area of north Sunnyvale, California, and the most interesting verified fact about it is that Equinix does not own it. The City of Sunnyvale parcel service returns assessor parcel 110-14-200 at this record's coordinates, with a situs of 444 Toyama Drive, Sunnyvale 94089, and the city's assessor sourced parcel layer records the same parcel under 438 Toyama Drive with a construction year of 1998, two storeys, 42,083 square feet of county recorded building area on 98,446 square feet of land, about 2.26 acres. The registered owner is Toyama Technology Partners LLC, with a mailing address at 2765 Sand Hill Road, Suite 200, Menlo Park, and a transfer recorded on 20 September 2021. As of the August 2025 assessor update the parcel carried a land value of $17,764,621 and an improvement value of $9,412,914, a total of $27,177,535. Land worth nearly twice the building is a fair summary of what Silicon Valley real estate does to a 1998 shell.

The Sand Hill Road address belongs to Menlo Equities, and reporting in February 2026 on a separate Menlo Equities data centre project at 888 to 894 Ross Drive in Sunnyvale noted in passing that the firm already owns a Sunnyvale data centre at 444 Toyama Drive, bought from Digital Realty in 2021. That matches the parcel transfer date exactly. So SV6 is a leased building in a landlord's portfolio, which is a large part of why Equinix publishes so little about it.

Equinix was founded in Silicon Valley in 1998 by two former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers on the premise that competing networks needed neutral ground to interconnect. It is headquartered in Redwood City, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015, and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Its Silicon Valley footprint spans San Jose, Santa Clara, Palo Alto and Sunnyvale, and it markets the region as its densest interconnection cluster. It does not publish SV6's square footage, its IT capacity, its utility service or its standby generation, and a fetch of the SV6 page returns none of those. The only floor area available for this building is the county's 42,083 square feet, which is an assessor's measure of the shell rather than an operator's statement of white space.

One correction is worth recording, because this registry previously carried it wrong. Sunnyvale is not served by Silicon Valley Power. Silicon Valley Power is the City of Santa Clara's own municipal utility and its service area is 18.41 square miles covering Santa Clara. Sunnyvale sits in Pacific Gas and Electric's distribution territory and is one of the thirteen communities served by Silicon Valley Clean Energy, the community choice aggregator that procures the generation while PG&E owns and maintains the lines and issues a single combined bill. Sunnyvale's constraint is therefore a PG&E interconnection constraint rather than a municipal one, and the scale of what that means locally shows in the Ross Drive project, where the developer secured 49 megawatts and an adjacent PG&E substation.

What is not known: SV6's IT load, its utility service capacity, its standby generation, its white space area, its year of first data centre fit out as distinct from the building's 1998 construction, and its tenants. Nothing in this row asserts any of them.

profile.capacity_note: Equinix publishes no power figure for SV6 under any of the four headings. There is no stated IT load, no utility service capacity, no standby generation rating and no on site generation. Certification and redundancy claims that appear on Equinix regional pages are written for the Silicon Valley portfolio as a whole and are not confirmed for this building, so none is recorded here. The only size figure available is the county assessor 42,083 square feet of building area, which measures the shell and not the technical space.
profile.research_note: Corrected 2026-09-05. The prior reading stated that Silicon Valley Power is Sunnyvale municipal utility. That is wrong. Silicon Valley Power is the City of Santa Clara municipal utility with an 18.41 square mile service area, and Sunnyvale is served by Pacific Gas and Electric with generation from Silicon Valley Clean Energy. City of Sunnyvale parcel service returns APN 110-14-200 at the stored coordinates, situs 444 Toyama Drive, county parcel record showing 438 Toyama Drive, year built 1998, two storeys, 42,083 square feet of building on 98,446 square feet of land, owner Toyama Technology Partners LLC at Menlo Equities Sand Hill Road address, transfer 20 September 2021. Equinix publishes no per building specs, so none are stored.
profile.community_note: The building is owned by Toyama Technology Partners LLC, an entity whose mailing address is Menlo Equities offices at 2765 Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, with the transfer recorded on 20 September 2021. Reporting in February 2026 on a separate Menlo Equities project at 888 to 894 Ross Drive in Sunnyvale, where the developer switched an approved 400,000 square foot office scheme to a two storey data centre with an adjacent Pacific Gas and Electric substation and had secured 49 megawatts of power, noted that the firm already owned the data centre at 444 Toyama Drive, purchased from Digital Realty in 2021. As of the August 2025 assessor update the parcel carried $17,764,621 of land value against $9,412,914 of improvement value.
profile.regulatory_note: Siting jurisdiction is the City of Sunnyvale. The parcel is assessor parcel 110-14-200, zoned MS with combining district ITRR3, in the Lakewood planning area, flood zone X, within the Sunnyvale Elementary and Fremont Union High school districts. The parcel is not in the Moffett Park Specific Plan area. Electricity is delivered by Pacific Gas and Electric, and generation is supplied by Silicon Valley Clean Energy, the community choice aggregator serving thirteen Santa Clara County communities including Sunnyvale, with PG&E maintaining the lines and issuing the combined bill.
profile.regional_context: Equinix was founded in Silicon Valley in 1998 and is headquartered in Redwood City. It converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Its Silicon Valley interconnection footprint spans San Jose, Santa Clara, Palo Alto and Sunnyvale. Sunnyvale, unlike neighbouring Santa Clara, has no municipal electric utility, and is served by Pacific Gas and Electric for delivery and Silicon Valley Clean Energy for generation.

reading.body:
Equinix SV6 is one of twelve facilities in Silicon Valley under Equinix's control, serving over 10,500 customers across enterprises and network providers, though the operator publishes no power consumption or capacity figures for individual buildings.

Equinix's opacity about per-facility power draw is typical among the largest colocation operators. The company discloses regional footprints and customer counts but withholds the specific megawatts consumed at each site, forcing researchers to infer capacity from real estate footprint or industry estimates rather than direct measurement. This matters because data center power consumption is the most direct proxy for AI training and inference infrastructure, yet remains largely proprietary.

SV6 sits in Sunnyvale, part of Equinix's larger Silicon Valley campus that spans multiple cities. The facility's location in the Bay Area situates it within the highest-density AI and cloud computing market in the United States. Whether SV6 runs at full power utilization, and how much of that power goes to AI workloads versus other tenants, remains unknown from published sources.

The gap between what Equinix discloses and what the compute constraint requires is significant. Understanding whether the grid binding constraint is real demands megawatt counts by facility and by customer. Until operators publish this data, estimates of AI scaling's power ceiling rest on aggregated utility filings and inference from acquisition announcements rather than operational fact.
